text: I am comparing Q’s LMI-designed balanced incentive game and mean-square best-response dynamics with P’s sampled CVaR zeroth-order optimization. I will first test whether P’s risk objective can be implemented by Q’s mechanism assumptions, then examine whether its sampling/communication method yields a genuinely new stability statement. I will cite exact paper lines and report obstructions.

I am testing whether Q’s quadratic tax and strong-monotonicity argument extend to risk-adjusted valuations \(V_n(x_n)=-\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta_n}(J_n(x_n,\xi_n))\), with P supplying a black-box empirical CVaR oracle. I will check Q’s exact curvature and sample-error requirements against P’s assumptions, and look for a smaller theorem or counterexample if a direct algorithm transplant fails.

A direct transplant of P’s Algorithm 1 into Q is invalid: P (Preliminaries and Eq. (update y)) has every agent maintain a copy of one common decision \(x\in\mathcal X\), and proves consensus; Q (manager problem (1)) optimizes heterogeneous allocations \((x_1,\ldots,x_N)\) under \(\sum_n x_n\le c\). Consensus can destroy welfare: for \(V_1(x)=2x-x^2/2\), \(V_2(x)=x-x^2/2\), \(c=1\), the optimum is \((1,0)\), while equal allocations \((1/2,1/2)\) lose \(1/4\). P also assumes \(r\mathbb B\subseteq\mathcal X\), incompatible with Q’s nonnegative allocation sets if copied literally. The reusable object is P’s empirical-CVaR oracle/error bound, not its consensus iteration.

Sharpened question: can Q’s quadratic tax implement a risk-aware allocation when only P’s black-box sampled losses are available, with quantitative economic guarantees for the true CVaR game? Use P’s expected empirical CVaR plus ball smoothing as a fixed convex surrogate, add \(\gamma\|x_n\|^2/2\) to ensure Q’s strong concavity, and normalize each valuation at \(x_n=0\). P’s bounded-loss DKW lemma (Appendix, Lemma cvar-estimation error bound) gives uniform-in-point \(h_n=L_n\delta_n+U_n\sqrt{2\pi}/(\beta_n\sqrt{s_n})\) value error. Conditional on Q’s tax/LMI certificate for the surrogate, its unique equilibrium has true planner loss at most \(2\sum_n h_n\), true unilateral regret at most \(4h_n\), exact payment balance, and true individual utility at least \(-2h_n\). This is a candidate theorem, not yet checked for the oracle-domain and Q proof issues. Emmy’s #3 correctly rules out importing P’s consensus iteration; I intend to use only its local CVaR estimator.

Major correction to my #4: Q’s advertised LMI certificate is algebraically infeasible. Q Theorem nash_implementation_theorem, P2(i) (inputs/Q.tex around 240–250) requires \(\sum_m A_{nm}^n=0\) for every \(n\). Q Proposition existence_uniqueness_prop, P1(ii) (around 200–213) requires \(\Psi+\Psi^\top\preceq-\upsilon I\) with \(\upsilon>0\), and its price-price block in row \(n,m\) is \(-A_{nm}^n\). Set a nonzero direction \(v\) with every allocation component zero and every price component the same \(h\). Then \(v^\top\Psi v=-\sum_n h^\top(\sum_m A_{nm}^n)h=0\), hence \(v^\top(\Psi+\Psi^\top)v=0\), contradicting strict negativity. Thus no tax can satisfy Q’s stated P1 and P2 LMIs jointly, including Eq. (40); Q Proposition prop2 is false as stated. This does not by itself disprove equilibrium uniqueness via another argument. It blocks invoking Q’s strong-monotonicity certificate for the proposed CVaR hybrid. I am checking whether a narrower value-stability result survives without that certificate.

Critical check on Q: its proposed payment (Eq. (40)) cannot satisfy its own strict P1 LMI (Eq. (existence_uniqueness_cond_eq)), despite Proposition (prop2). For any \(N\ge2\), its price-dependent own-price derivative is \(\partial_{p_n}U_n=-\alpha[p_n-\bar p_{-n}/(N-1)]+\alpha(\sum_m x_m-c)/(N-1)\). Holding \(x\) fixed and moving all prices by the same vector \(h\) leaves this pseudogradient component unchanged. Thus the price-price Jacobian has common-price null vector \((h,\ldots,h)\), so the full symmetric pseudogradient Jacobian has zero quadratic form on \((\Delta x=0,\Delta p=(h,\ldots,h))\); it cannot be \(\preceq-\upsilon I\) for \(\upsilon>0\). This blocks using Q’s claimed explicit LMI certificate as a theorem. It does not by itself prove nonunique NE; a different uniqueness proof or redesigned tax is needed. P’s CVaR oracle still provides a separate route to quantitative approximate-equilibrium guarantees.

Beyond the LMI contradiction in #5/#6, Eq. (40) can have genuinely nonunique Nash equilibria. Take \(N=2,K=1,c=2,\mathcal X_1=\mathcal X_2=[0,1],\alpha=1\), and \(V_n(x)=2x-x^2/2\). For each \(p\in[0,1]\), the profile \((x_1,p_1,x_2,p_2)=(1,p,1,p)\) is NE. Directly from Q Eq. (40), \(\partial_{x_n}U_n=V_n\prime(x_n)+p_n-2p_{-n}\), \(\partial_{p_n}U_n=-p_n+p_{-n}+x_1+x_2-c\), and the own-strategy Hessian is \(\begin{psmallmatrix}-1&1\\1&-1\end{psmallmatrix}\preceq0\). At the profile, these derivatives are \(1-p\ge0\) at upper bound \(x_n=1\), and \(0\) for price, proving a global best response. Thus Q’s claimed unique NE fails under its stated compact, strongly concave valuation assumptions; optimum allocation remains unique. This is compatible with P’s genuinely stochastic risk model: let \(\xi=\pm 1/4\) equiprobably, \(J_n(x,\xi)=x^2/2-(9/4+\xi)x\), and take tail level \(\beta=1/2\); then \(\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}J_n(x,\xi)=x^2/2-2x\) on \([0,1]\). P’s bounded convex Lipschitz sample-loss assumptions hold on this compact set. I will put the derivation in ada/.

Despite #5–6, Q Eq. (40) appears to admit a direct full-implementation proof without strict monotonicity. For each resource \(k\), write \(P^k=\sum_n p_n^k\) and \(z^k=\sum_n x_n^k-c^k\). Q’s tax gives \(\partial_{p_n^k}U_n=-\alpha(Np_n^k-P^k-z^k)/(N-1)\). At a price best response, if any \(p_n^k>0\), then \(Np_n^k=P^k+z^k>0\), forcing every price positive/equal and then \(z^k=0\) by summation. If all prices vanish, the boundary derivative condition gives \(z^k\le0\). Hence every NE has common \(p^k\ge0\), feasible allocations, and \(p^k z^k=0\). At common prices, \(\partial_{x_n}t_n=\alpha p\), so each allocation best response maximizes \(V_n(x_n)-\alpha p^\top x_n\). These are precisely planner KKT conditions with \(\lambda=\alpha p\), proving every NE allocation optimal for concave \(V_n\), even nonsmooth via subgradients. Conversely a planner primal-dual pair yields an NE (assuming a multiplier exists). Q’s unique-message claim fails: \(N=2,K=1,\mathcal X_n=[0,1],c=2,V_n(x)=2x-x^2/2,\alpha=1\) has \(x_1=x_2=1\) and any common \(p\in[0,1]\) as NE. This outcome-only theorem is the safer foundation for combining Q with P’s CVaR oracle.

Qualification to #8: the converse from planner primal-dual pair to a Nash equilibrium needs Q’s \(\alpha\)-strong concavity (or another condition making each player’s objective jointly concave in \((x_n,p_n)\)), not mere concavity. In Eq. (40), the own \((x_n,p_n)\) cross coefficient is \(\alpha/(N-1)\), while the own price curvature is \(-\alpha\). Combining Q’s \(-\alpha\) curvature in \(x_n\) gives a negative semidefinite own Hessian for \(N\ge2\); then the first-order conditions suffice. The forward statement, every existing NE allocates optimally, only needs concavity of the planner valuation and the price best-response identities.

Further correction: Q Eq. (40) also fails its individual-rationality claim under stated assumptions. Let \(N=2,K=1,c=1,\mathcal X_n=[0,1],\alpha=1\), \(V_1(x)=4x-x^2/2\), \(V_2(x)=x-x^2/2\). The social optimum is \((x_1,x_2)=(1,0)\). At common price \(p_1=p_2=3\), all price derivatives vanish; \(\partial_{x_1}U_1=V_1\prime(1)-3=0\), \(\partial_{x_2}U_2=V_2\prime(0)-3=-2\le0\), and own utilities are jointly concave, so this is an NE. Substitution into Q Eq. (40) gives \(t_1=3p(x_1-c/2)=9/2\), whereas \(V_1(1)=7/2\); hence \(U_1=-1<0=V_1(0)\). The IR proof’s proposed zero-demand deviation also fails: holding prices and rival fixed, \(t_1((0,3),(0,3))=3/2>0\). This can arise from P-compatible CVaR losses \(J_n(x,\xi)=x^2/2-(b_n+1/4+\xi)x\), \(b_1=4,b_2=1\), \(\xi=\pm1/4\) equiprobably, tail \(\beta=1/2\). Thus my #4 candidate theorem must drop exact/approximate IR for Eq. (40), unless a redesigned transfer rule is proved. Exact budget balance and optimal allocation still survive. I will document this counterexample in ada/.

Further failure of Q Eq. (40): individual rationality can fail at a genuine NE. Let \(N=2,K=1,\mathcal X_1=\mathcal X_2=[0,1],c=1,\alpha=0.1\), \(V_1(x)=1.1x-0.05x^2\), \(V_2(x)=0.5x-0.05x^2\). The planner optimum is \((1,0)\), with multiplier \(\lambda=1\); Eq. (40) has an NE at \((x_1,x_2,p_1,p_2)=(1,0,10,10)\). Indeed the own payoff Hessian is \(\begin{psmallmatrix}-0.1&0.1\\0.1&-0.1\end{psmallmatrix}\preceq0\), and at this profile price derivatives vanish, agent 1’s allocation derivative is \(V_1\prime(1)-1=0\), agent 2’s is \(V_2\prime(0)-1=-0.5\) at lower bound. Direct substitution in Eq. (40) gives \(t_1=1.5\), \(t_2=-1.5\). Thus \(U_1=V_1(1)-t_1=1.05-1.5=-0.45<0=V_1(0)\), contradicting Q’s P4/Proposition (prop2). P-compatible stochastic losses realizing these valuations are \(J_1(x,\xi)=0.05x^2-(1.2+\xi)x\), \(J_2(x,\xi)=0.05x^2-(0.6+\xi)x\), with \(\xi=\pm0.1\) equiprobably and CVaR upper-tail level \(\beta=1/2\); then \(-\operatorname{CVaR}_{1/2}J_n=V_n\) on \([0,1]\), and each sample loss is convex, bounded, Lipschitz. A Q–P synthesis should target efficient allocations and budget balance first, then redesign transfers if exact IR is required.

Proposed exact repair of Q Eq. (40) IR, without changing any best response: write \(\kappa_N=(N^2-N+1)/(N-1)^2=1+N/(N-1)^2\). Direct substitution at any common-price complementary NE gives \(t_n=\alpha\kappa_N p^\top(x_n-c/N)\) (terms involving \(p^\top(\sum_mx_m-c)\) vanish). Add the others-only rebate \(R_n(s_{-n})=\alpha(\kappa_N-1)(\bar p_{-n}/(N-1))^\top(\bar x_{-n}-(N-1)c/N)\), and define \(t_n^\mathrm{new}=t_n+R_n\). At NE, \(\bar p_{-n}/(N-1)=p\) and \(\bar x_{-n}=c-x_n\) in every priced coordinate, so \(t_n^\mathrm{new}=\alpha p^\top(x_n-c/N)\). Hence \(\sum_n t_n^\mathrm{new}=0\) and \(U_n^\mathrm{new}\ge V_n(0)+\alpha p^\top c/N\ge0\), since \(x_n\) maximizes \(V_n(x_n)-\alpha p^\top x_n\) and \(0\in\mathcal X_n\). The rebate uses no \(s_n\), so NE set and efficient allocation are unchanged. Need check the formula carefully for slack coordinates and transfer signs; this could be the constructive Q–P line once paired with P’s CVaR surrogate oracle.

Transfer repair for Q Eq. (40), independent of valuation reports: at any NE, price complementarity from #8 gives \(p_n=p\), \(\lambda=\alpha p\), and \(p^\top(\sum_mx_m-c)=0\). Direct simplification of Eq. (40) gives \(t_n=A_N\lambda^\top(x_n-c/N)\), with \(A_N=(N^2-N+1)/(N-1)^2=1+N/(N-1)^2\). Define an added payment depending only on others’ messages, \(g_n(s_{-n})=\alpha N/(N-1)^3\,\bar p_{-n}^\top[\bar x_{-n}-(N-1)c/N]\), and \(t_n^{\rm new}=t_n+g_n\). Since \(g_n\) is independent of \(s_n\), the entire NE set and all best responses are unchanged. At every NE, complementarity gives \(g_n=(1-A_N)\lambda^\top(x_n-c/N)\), hence \(t_n^{\rm new}=\lambda^\top(x_n-c/N)\). Thus \(\sum_n t_n^{\rm new}=\lambda^\top(\sum_nx_n-c)=0\), and \(U_n^{\rm new}=V_n(x_n)-\lambda^\top x_n+\lambda^\top c/N\ge V_n(0)+\lambda^\top c/N\ge V_n(0)\), because each \(x_n\) maximizes \(V_n(x_n)-\lambda^\top x_n\) and \(0\in\mathcal X_n\). This appears to restore exact IR and BB without changing Q’s efficient equilibrium allocations; I am checking algebra and edge cases.

Sharper structural theorem for Q Eq. (40) and the repaired tax in #12–13: assume \(N\ge2\), \(0\in\mathcal X_n\) compact convex, \(V_n\) upper semicontinuous and \(\alpha\)-strongly concave, and existence of a planner multiplier. Then the NE set is exactly \(\{(x^\star,p_1=\cdots=p_N=\lambda/\alpha):\lambda\in\Lambda^\star\}\), where \(x^\star\) is the unique welfare-maximizing allocation and \(\Lambda^\star\) is the (possibly non-singleton) optimal multiplier set. Necessity follows from price best responses and allocation best responses (#8). Sufficiency follows because each player’s payoff is jointly concave in \((x_n,p_n)\): Q’s strong curvature gives own Hessian bounded by \(\alpha\begin{psmallmatrix}-I&I/(N-1)\\I/(N-1)&-I\end{psmallmatrix}\preceq0\), so KKT conditions imply a global best response. The others-only repair preserves this set and proves BB+IR for every equilibrium, including nonunique prices. Thus the correct dynamic target is the equilibrium set or unique allocation, not a unique message profile.

Quantitative Q–P synthesis conditional on solving the learning step: for each agent let \(C_n(x)=\operatorname{CVaR}_{\beta_n}J_n(x,\xi_n)\), \(H_{n,s}(x)=\mathbb E[\widehat C_{n,s}(x)]\) for a fresh size-\(s_n\) empirical CVaR batch, and normalized valuations \(V_n(x)=u_n(x)-C_n(x)-[u_n(0)-C_n(0)]\), \(\widetilde V_n(x)=u_n(x)-H_{n,s}(x)-[u_n(0)-H_{n,s}(0)]\). If P’s sample losses are convex, \(L_n\)-Lipschitz and bounded by \(U_n\), and \(u_n\) is \(\alpha\)-strongly concave, both valuations are \(\alpha\)-strongly concave. P Appendix CVaR-stability lemma plus its DKW integration gives \(\sup_x|H_{n,s}(x)-C_n(x)|\le\kappa_n:=U_n\sqrt{2\pi}/(\beta_n\sqrt{s_n})\); this is a deterministic bound on the expected surrogate, with no uniform-over-samples claim. Thus \(\sup_x|V_n-\widetilde V_n|\le\varepsilon_n:=2\kappa_n\). Run Q Eq. (40) with the others-only transfer repair #13 for the surrogate game. At any surrogate NE \(\widetilde s\), the true planner welfare gap is at most \(2\sum_n\varepsilon_n=4\sum_n\kappa_n\); true unilateral gain from any deviation is at most \(2\varepsilon_n=4\kappa_n\); total payments are exactly zero; and true utility is at least \(-\varepsilon_n=-2\kappa_n\) relative to the normalized outside option. Strong concavity further gives \(\|\widetilde x-x^\star\|\le2\sqrt{\sum_n\varepsilon_n/\alpha}\). These are direct two-sided value perturbation bounds plus #14, not consequences of P’s consensus theorem. If \(J_n(0,\xi)=0\) a.s., normalization adds no extra error and every factor \(2\) from \(\varepsilon_n=2\kappa_n\) drops.

Narrow prior-work check (not a novelty claim): searched `site:arxiv.org risk averse CVaR mechanism design budget balance Nash implementation resource allocation`, `site:arxiv.org conditional value at risk mechanism design distributed resource allocation Nash equilibrium budget balanced`, `site:arxiv.org zeroth order CVaR generalized Nash equilibrium stochastic aggregative game`, `"CVaR" "budget balanced" mechanism design resource allocation`, and `"CVaR" "Nash implementation" mechanism design`. Relevant adjacent papers found: Dahlin–Jain, https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.06119, includes CVaR in a two-stage market but explicitly assumes nonstrategic agents for its market mechanism (abstract); Du–Meng, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.06023, gives distributed learning for stochastic aggregative games under expectation-valued costs and strong monotonicity (abstract), assumptions unavailable for Q’s Eq. (40) because #5–6. These do not establish novelty of our repaired-tax plus CVaR-oracle direction; a fuller literature review remains.

My #4 overstated the true-game regret and assumed IR from the original tax. After the others-only repair #12–13, the bounds sharpen because valuation normalization constants cancel in comparisons: if \(\sup_x|\widetilde C_n(x)-C_n(x)|\le h_n\), then a surrogate NE has true unilateral regret \(\le2h_n\) and true planner loss \(\le2\sum_nh_n\), although \(\sup_x|\widetilde V_n-V_n|\le2h_n\). True individual utility is \(\ge-2h_n\), and transfers balance exactly. With P’s fixed-sample expected empirical CVaR plus smoothing, \(h_n=L_n\delta_n+U_n\sqrt{2\pi}/(\beta_n\sqrt{s_n})\) under oracle access on a \(\delta_n\)-neighborhood. The precise derivation, Q counterexamples, tax repair, and remaining dynamic gap are in ada/pair_note.md; both style checks pass. This refines #15’s generic factors by exploiting cancellation, and includes smoothing needed for Q-style gradient play.

Sharpening #15 after cross-checking ada/pair_note.md: the normalization constants cancel when comparing two allocations or a unilateral deviation. Let \(d_n(x)=H_{n,s}(x)-C_n(x)\), with \(|d_n(x)|\le\kappa_n\). Then \((V_n-\widetilde V_n)(x)=d_n(x)-d_n(0)\), so differences between two decisions have magnitude at most \(2\kappa_n\), not \(4\kappa_n\). Consequently the true welfare gap at a surrogate NE is \(\le2\sum_n\kappa_n\), true unilateral regret is \(\le2\kappa_n\), and strong concavity gives \(\|\widetilde x-x^\star\|\le2\sqrt{\sum_n\kappa_n/\alpha}\). The true IR shortfall remains \(\le2\kappa_n\), since it compares normalized utility with zero. Ada’s note has these sharper factors; #15 remains valid but loose. The same cancellation holds with P’s smoothing term \(h_n=L_n\delta_n+\kappa_n\) wherever its queries are feasible.

An additional dynamic-evidence mismatch in Q: Theorem theorem4 (inputs/Q.tex around lines 518–523) assumes \(Q_i=\lceil C_b/\eta^{2(i+1)}\rceil\) with \(0<\eta<1\), so sample size grows geometrically. Its numerical section (around lines 678–685) instead says \(Q_i=\lceil\widetilde\eta^{i+1}\rceil\) with \(\widetilde\eta=0.96\), which equals \(1\) at every iteration. Thus the plotted trajectories do not instantiate the theorem’s sampling regime as written. This reinforces that a Q–P paper should prove its own learning statement; P’s fixed-batch result targets a shared decision and cannot certify Q’s game.

Scope and remaining gap for a publication: I sharpened the pair question from “is there a connection?” to “can an efficient, balanced, individually rational resource-allocation mechanism be learned from black-box CVaR losses with a finite-sample economic guarantee?” The static answer is the repaired-tax theorem (#14, #18; also ada/pair_note.md). P’s objective is the sum/average of individual CVaRs (P Preliminaries and Appendix remark), so this does not optimize \(\operatorname{CVaR}(\sum_nJ_n)\) in general. A full paper still needs a decentralized zeroth-order or primal-dual learning theorem for Q’s heterogeneous allocations, with feasible perturbation queries near nonnegative boundaries, and convergence to the equilibrium set despite nonunique prices and lack of Q’s strict monotonicity. P’s exact-consensus theorem solves a different shared-decision problem and cannot supply that step. Fixed fresh-batch expected empirical CVaR is a deterministic surrogate; its value bound alone does not prove that an implementable strategic learning rule reaches its equilibrium. Q also allows interim capacity violations because its allocation rule is \(y_n=x_n\) and feasibility emerges only at equilibrium. The prior-work search in #16 was narrow, so novelty is unresolved.
ready at #20

Final independent account is in ada/pair_note.md (style-gates and local artifact ban both pass). Q Eq. (40) has efficient equilibrium allocations but its claimed strict P1 LMI is incompatible with P2(i); prices need not be unique, and original transfers can violate IR (#5, #7, #10). The others-only rebate in #12 restores exact equilibrium budget balance and IR without changing best responses; I checked the general coefficient algebra for several \(N\) and the explicit IR counterexample numerically. Pairing that repaired tax with P’s fixed fresh-batch expected empirical CVaR plus smoothing yields a deterministic surrogate with \(h_n=L_n\delta_n+U_n\sqrt{2\pi}/(\beta_n\sqrt{s_n})\) pointwise value error, hence true welfare loss \(\le2\sum_nh_n\), true unilateral regret \(\le2h_n\), and true utility \(\ge-2h_n\) at any surrogate NE, conditional on an oracle neighborhood and a planner multiplier. Exact dynamic convergence from P’s samples remains unproved: P’s consensus theorem addresses a shared decision, whereas Q has separate coupled allocations and nonunique prices. Emmy’s #20 agrees on this boundary. No claim of publication novelty follows from this pair alone.
ready at #22

Reopened after ada #22 and independently checked its core algebra against Q Eq. (40), lines 412–422, and P Appendix CVaR/DKW bound, lines 1287–1315. At a common-price complementary equilibrium, Q’s original tax is \(t_n=\alpha[1+N/(N-1)^2]p^\top(x_n-c/N)\). The others-only rebate in #13 therefore leaves every best response intact and reduces the equilibrium tax to \(\alpha p^\top(x_n-c/N)\), giving exact balance and participation when \(0\in\mathcal X_n\) and valuations are normalized. P’s \(2U/\beta\) CVaR CDF bound and integrated DKW bound yield \(U\sqrt{2\pi}/(\beta\sqrt{s})\) in expected absolute value at each point; because this constant is point-independent, the expected empirical surrogate obeys the deterministic bound used by ada. The sharper \(2h_n\) regret and \(2\sum_nh_n\) welfare bounds in #17/#22 follow by canceling valuation-normalization constants. I found no new obstruction to the static theorem. Dynamic convergence, feasible perturbation queries, multiplier existence, and literature novelty remain unresolved; P’s common-decision consensus theorem does not discharge them.
ready at #24

Final source cross-check: Q Eq. (40), inputs/Q.tex lines 410–422, gives the price derivative and common-price equilibrium tax in ada/pair_note.md; Q P1(ii) and P2(i), lines 200–250, still contradict along a common-price direction. P Assumptions Lipschitz/convex, inputs/P.tex lines 495–511, and its Appendix CVaR/DKW estimate, lines 1287–1315, support the expected empirical surrogate and pointwise error \(h_n=L_n\delta_n+U_n\sqrt{2\pi}/(\beta_n\sqrt{s_n})\), provided queries are possible on the full perturbation neighborhood. The rebate is independent of agent \(n\) messages, so the Q equilibrium set stays fixed; it yields true welfare gap \(\le 2\sum_n h_n\) and unilateral regret \(\le 2h_n\) by cancellation of normalization constants. I found no new obstruction to this static theorem. Implementable convergence, feasible perturbation queries, multiplier existence, and novelty remain unresolved; P Algorithm 1 uses consensus over one common decision, not Q heterogeneous coupled allocations.
ready at #26

ITERATE: The connection is promising, but the note’s payment identity is wrong for general \(N\). Expanding Q’s Eq. (40) at equilibrium gives \(t_n=(N+1)\lambda^\top(x_n-c/N)/(N-1)^2\); the proposed rebate then gives \((t_n+g_n)=\lambda^\top(x_n-c/N)/(N-1)^2\), rather than the claimed coefficient \(1\). The ledger repeats the incorrect identity, so the transfer argument needs a fresh general-\(N\) check before the static result is drafted. Action: Recompute the equilibrium transfers for arbitrary \(N\), then verify budget balance and individual rationality using the corrected coefficient.

Verifier #28 is incorrect for Q Eq. (40), lines 412–422: it omits the third term’s factor \(N/(N-1)\). At common price \(p_m=p\), write \(z=\sum_mx_m-c\) and \(d_n=x_n-c/N\). The price-quadratic terms cancel, the third term is \(\alpha Np^\top d_n/(N-1)\), and the final term is \(\alpha[p^\top d_n-p^\top z]/(N-1)^2\). Thus \(t_n/\alpha=[N/(N-1)+1/(N-1)^2]p^\top d_n-[1/(N-1)+1/(N-1)^2]p^\top z\). At complementary equilibrium \(p^\top z=0\), the coefficient is \(\kappa_N=(N^2-N+1)/(N-1)^2\), as in #12–13 and ada/pair_note.md. The rebate in #13 contributes \(-\alpha Np^\top d_n/(N-1)^2\), leaving \(t_n^{\rm new}=\alpha p^\top d_n\), so balance and IR remain valid. For \(N=3,c=3,x=(2,1,0),p=1,n=1,\alpha=1\), Eq. (40) gives \(t_1=7/4\), rebate \(-3/4\), and revised transfer \(1\); #28 predicts \(1\) for the original tax and is contradicted directly.

Full general-\(N\) audit is in emmy/transfer_audit.md (style gate and artifact ban pass). It expands all five terms of Q Eq. (40), derives \(\kappa_N=(N^2-N+1)/(N-1)^2\), and checks the rebate leaves \(t_n^{\rm new}=\alpha p^\top(x_n-c/N)\), exact equilibrium budget balance, and IR. The \(N=3\) countercheck to verifier #28 is a genuine NE under Q assumptions: \(\mathcal X_n=[0,2]\), \(c=3\), \(\alpha=1\), \(V_1(x)=3x-x^2/2\), \(V_2(x)=2x-x^2/2\), \(V_3(x)=x/2-x^2/2\), \(x=(2,1,0)\), and all \(p_n=1\). Own payoff gradients satisfy KKT and the Hessian is negative definite; Q Eq. (40) gives \(t_1=7/4\), rebate \(-3/4\), revised tax \(1\). The coefficient in #28 instead predicts \(t_1=1\). Static Q–P conclusions in #17/#22 survive this audit; implementable learning and novelty remain unresolved.
ready at #30

Independent audit of verifier #28 agrees with emmy #29–30 and resolves the coefficient objection. From Q Eq. (40), at common price \(p\), set \(d_n=x_n-c/N\), \(z=\sum_mx_m-c\). The first and fourth terms cancel; the third contributes \(\alpha Np^\top d_n/(N-1)\), and the last contributes \(\alpha p^\top(d_n-z)/(N-1)^2\). With the second term, \(t_n/\alpha=\kappa_Np^\top d_n-Np^\top z/(N-1)^2\), where \(\kappa_N=(N^2-N+1)/(N-1)^2\).
